transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Um, yeah, so I guess I'm here because... well, things have just gotten completely out of hand lately. I recently finished my bachelor's degree, and I thought, you know, now I'll just step into the real world and do all the normal things you're supposed to do. But what finally made me actually come in today—which, honestly, it's a miracle I even made it here on time because I almost couldn't find my keys again—is that I just keep forgetting basic adult things. 

Like, really basic things that everyone else seems to manage without thinking. I'll have a bill sitting right on my kitchen counter, literally right next to my coffee mug so I can't possibly miss it, and I still forget to pay it until I get hit with a late fee. And it's not just bills, it's everything. I've been trying to find a job, obviously, but I'll get an email back from a recruiter for an interview, I'll read it on my phone, think to myself, "Oh, I need to reply to this as soon as I finish lunch," and then it completely vanishes from my brain. I've literally ghosted potential employers just because I completely forgot to return their interview emails. 

And showing up for appointments is a total disaster—I missed my dentist appointment last Tuesday because I swore it was Wednesday. And errands are just as bad, I never follow through on them. I'll go out to do one specific thing, like drop off a package, and I'll come back three hours later having done a million other random things but the package is still sitting in the passenger seat of my car. It's just... it's starting to cost me real opportunities, you know? Like, actual career opportunities, and money I really don't have right now, and I just feel like I'm completely failing at being a functional person.
Did you experience similar difficulties with focus and organization when you were growing up, before the age of twelve?

Oh, absolutely. Yeah, way before twelve. Like, even back in early elementary school, it was exactly the same. My mom actually kept all my old report cards in this big plastic tub in our basement, and if you read through them, it's like a broken record. Every single year, my teachers would write these little notes saying, you know, that I was a really bright girl and I had all this potential, but... then they'd list all the things I was doing wrong. 

I was constantly losing my worksheets. Literally, the teacher would hand a paper to the person in front of me, they'd pass it back to me, and somehow by the time we were supposed to work on it, mine was just gone. Vanished. And my desk—oh my gosh, my desk was an absolute disaster zone. It was just crammed full of crumpled up papers, old drawings, broken pencils, and God knows what else. It was so messy that I could never, ever find my assignments when it was time to turn them in. I'd be frantically digging through this black hole inside my desk while everyone else was already passing theirs to the front. 

And it wasn't just the losing things, either. I would always rush through the directions on everything. I just couldn't sit there and read step one, step two, step three... I'd just glance at it, guess what I was supposed to do, and speed through it. And I was always getting in trouble for talking out of turn, too. I just couldn't hold my thoughts in if I had something to say, so I'd just blurt it out in the middle of a lesson or interrupt the teacher. 

I remember my third-grade teacher actually tried to make me this special color-coded folder system to help me keep track of things, but I think I lost the folders within a week. It was just so frustrating because I really did want to be good and do it right, but I just couldn't. And honestly, looking back, it feels like nothing has changed since I was seven years old. It's just... it's bills and job interviews now instead of spelling worksheets, you know? But the feeling of just completely failing at keeping my life organized is exactly the same.
Do you often feel physically restless or have difficulty sitting still without needing to fidget or move around?

Oh, God, yes. Constantly. It's actually one of the things that makes trying to get a job right now so agonizing for me. Like, when I actually do remember to reply to an email and I manage to get an interview... sitting through it is just torture. I mean, I know I'm supposed to look professional and composed, but the whole time, I just feel this... this intense, buzzing pressure inside my body. It's like my bones are vibrating or something. 

If I have to sit still for more than, I don't know, ten minutes, whether it's an interview, or a meeting back when I was doing group projects in college, or honestly, even just sitting in a movie theater with my friends trying to watch a two-hour film... I just feel like I'm going to literally crawl out of my skin if I don't move. I have to shift my weight, or cross and uncross my legs, or bounce my knee. And my hands are always going. I'll be twisting a ring, or picking at my cuticles until they bleed, or clicking a pen if I have one—which I've been told is incredibly annoying, but I almost don't even realize I'm doing it until someone glares at me. 

It's just this overwhelming need to do *something* physical. It's like all that mental energy I can't organize just turns into physical electricity that has to go somewhere. I try so hard to suppress it, especially in professional settings, because I know it makes me look nervous or unprepared, but holding it in just makes the internal pressure worse until I feel like I'm holding my breath underwater. So yeah, sitting still is... it's really, really hard for me.

And my moods... I mean, I get frustrated, obviously, like when I lose my keys for the fourth time in a week or when I realize I missed a deadline, but I wouldn't say my mood swings wildly for no reason.
